# III.  Bayesian multi-level survival analysis for EFFECT OF SURGERY (surgery y/n) with random intercept for centre


## Set prior for beta variables
Set a neutral, weakly-regularising prior...
 ~ student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2.5)
```{r}
prior_beta_sx <- student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2, autoscale = c(FALSE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE))
```
NB needed to set a tighter scale variable for prior_intercept and also prior_beta_sx in order to improve regularisation and resolve divergent transitions.

Based on the DAG, use the following adjustment variables: age, clin signs, concurrent congen, pressure grad, referral centre, stenosis type.





## Fit model with for surgery (plus correction set)
NB use status ... rstanarm requires the dead animals to be classified as 1, whilst censored are 0.
```{r}
mod_sx <- stan_surv(formula = Surv(tstart, tstop, status) ~ surgery
                    + s_age
                    + concurrent_congenital
                    + type
                    + clinical_signs
                    + s_pv_max_pg
                    + (1| centre),
  data = df,
  basehaz = "ms",
  prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 10, autoscale = FALSE),
  prior = prior_beta_sx,
  prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
  iter    = 12000,
  warmup = 4000,
  chains = 4,
  cores = 4,
  adapt_delta = 0.9999,  # Often helpful for complex models
  seed = 666)
```



## Summarise priors from model
```{r}
prior_summary(mod_sx)
```



## Model summary
```{r}
summary(mod_sx)
```



## Model short summary
```{r}
print(mod_sx, digits = 3)
```




##  Plot Baseline hazard of model
```{r}
plot(mod_sx)
```





## Plots of model convergences

## Get results
```{r}
posterior_mod_sx <- as.array(mod_sx)
```





### a. Check trace plots for model
```{r}
color_scheme_set("mix-blue-pink")
mcmc_trace(posterior_mod_sx)
```




### b. Trace rank plot
```{r}
color_scheme_set("mix-blue-pink")
mcmc_rank_overlay(posterior_mod_sx) +
  ylim(c(300, 475))
```



### c. get dens overlay plot for chains
```{r}
color_scheme_set("blue")
mcmc_dens_overlay(posterior_mod_sx)
```



## Summaries of coefficients

### a. HPDI for the different beta parameters
```{r}
draws <- as.matrix(mod_sx)
median(draws[,2]) # draws for surgery
HPDI(draws[,2], 0.97) # draws for surgery
HPDI(draws[,2], 0.89) # draws for surgery
```



### b. Hypothesis tests on beta parameters
#### surgery
probability that effect is negative
```{r}
mean(draws[,2] < 0) # draws for surgery
```




### c. Plot posterior distribution for beta coefficient of surgery
```{r}
s_sx <- draws[,2] # 2nd column is draws for surgery

ggplot(data.frame(s_sx), aes(x = s_sx)) +
  geom_density(fill = "orange", alpha = 0.7) +
  labs(title = "Posterior of beta coefficient for intervention",
       x = "Beta coefficient",
       y = "Density") +
  theme_bw() +
           theme(axis.title.y = element_text(size=16, face="bold"), 
               axis.title.x = element_text(size=14, face="bold"),
               title = element_text(size=14, face="bold"),
               plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
               axis.text.x = element_text(color = "grey50", size = 12),
               axis.text.y = element_text(color = "grey50",size = 12)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype="dotted", 
                color = "firebrick", linewidth = 1.5)  +
                ylim(0, 1.5) +
                xlim(-2.0, 2.0)
```








## Get HDI for coefficients
```{r}
hdi <- bayestestR::hdi(mod_sx, ci = c(0.50, 0.68, 0.89, 0.97), parameters = "surgery")
plot(hdi)
```



## Get density plots for posterior distributons of beta parameters
```{r}
mcmc_dens(posterior_mod_sx,
  pars = c("surgery1"))
```



## Get area plot for posterior distributons of beta parameters
```{r}
mcmc_areas(posterior_mod_sx,
  pars = "surgery1")
```



## Calculate hazard ratios for surgery
### a. get posterior draws
```{r}
surgery_hr <- exp(draws[,2]) # 2nd column is draws for surgery)
```



### b. Summarise hazard ratios for surgery
```{r}
median(surgery_hr)
hpdi_surgery <- HPDI(surgery_hr, prob = c(0.89, 0.97))
hpdi_surgery
```



### c. Plot posterior distribution for hazard ratio of surgery
```{r}
ggplot(data.frame(surgery_hr), aes(x = surgery_hr)) +
  geom_density(fill = "lightblue", alpha = 0.7) +
  labs(title = "Posterior distribution of hazard ratio for intervention",
       x = "Hazard Ratio",
       y = "Density") +
  theme_bw() +
           theme(axis.title.y = element_text(size=12, face="bold"), 
               axis.title.x = element_text(size=12, face="bold"),
               title = element_text(size=14, face="bold"),
               plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
               axis.text.x = element_text(color = "grey50", size = 12),
               axis.text.y = element_text(color = "grey50",size = 12)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype="dotted", 
                color = "firebrick", linewidth = 1.5) +
  xlim(0, 4)
```





### 2. Check performance of prior probability
```{r}
mod_sx_prior_only <- update(mod_sx, prior_PD = TRUE) 
```







### 3. Check prosterior vs prior for beta variable
#### a. extract draws for posterior and prior
```{r}
# extract draws
post_draws  <- as.matrix(mod_sx)
prior_draws <- as.matrix(mod_sx_prior_only)
```





#### b. plot marginal distributions for posterior and prior
``` {r}
# Compare marginal distributions
dens(post_draws[, "surgery1"], show.zero = TRUE, col = "red", main = "Neutral prior v posterior for intervention", xlab = "Beta coefficient for the effect of intervention", xlim = c(-2, 2), ylim = c(0, 1.8)) 
dens(prior_draws[, "surgery1"], add=TRUE, col = "blue", show.zero = TRUE)
```



#### c. compute prior tail probability of posterior mean
If this probability is very small (e.g. < 0.05), the posterior lies in a region the prior considered implausible.
```{r}
beta_hat <- mean(post_draws[, "surgery1"])

mean(abs(prior_draws[, "surgery1"] - beta_hat) <
       abs(prior_draws[, "surgery1"] - mean(prior_draws[, "surgery1"])))

```





### 4. Sensitivity analyses to assess robustness of results to choice of prior
#### a. create priors of different strength for surgery1 variable
To determine whether the substantive conclusions depend upon the exact prior choice.

NB the scale variable is strengthened or weakened by multiplying or dividing the scale of the main prior by 2, respectively. The location is set to the posterior mean from the main model, to ensure that the priors are centred on a plausible value.
```{r}
priors_bin <- list(
  weak = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2.5, autoscale = c(FALSE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE)),
  moderate = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 1.25, autoscale = c(FALSE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE)),
  strong = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 0.625, autoscale = c(FALSE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE))
)
```



#### b. refit model with different priors and compare results
```{r}
fits <- lapply(priors_bin, function(p) {
  stan_surv(formula = Surv(tstart, tstop, status) ~ surgery
                    + s_age
                    + concurrent_congenital
                    + type
                    + clinical_signs
                    + s_pv_max_pg
                    + (1| centre),
            basehaz = "ms",
            data = df,
            prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 10, autoscale = FALSE),
            prior = p,
            prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
            iter    = 2000,
            chains = 4,
            cores = 4,
            adapt_delta = 0.9999,  # Often helpful for complex models
            seed = 666
            )
})
```



#### c. compare posterior intervals for hazard ratios for intervention across different priors
```{r}
# calculate median hazard ratio across different priors
HR_med_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  posterior::as_draws_df(f) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    summarise(
      median = exp(quantile(surgery1, probs = 0.5))
    )
})
HR_med <- c(HR_med_sens[[1]], HR_med_sens[[2]], HR_med_sens[[3]])


# calculate 89% credible interval for hazard ratio across different priors
HR_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  exp(posterior_interval(f, pars = "surgery1", prob = 0.89))
})

# combine median and credible intervals into a summary table
HR_sens_summary <- rbind(HR_med, HR_sens)
row.names(HR_sens_summary) <- c("Median", "Lower", "Upper")

# transpose the table for better readability
HR_sens_summary
```








## Make model predictions and plot for surgery
### 1. Create new data where age differs
```{r}
nd <- data.frame(centre = rep("p", 2),
                 surgery = c(0, 1),
                 s_pv_max_pg = rep(0, 2),
                 concurrent_congenital = rep(0, 2),
                 type = rep("a", 2),
                 s_age = rep(0, 2),
                 clinical_signs = rep(0, 2)
                 )
head(nd)
```




### 2. Make posterior predictions from new data
```{r}
ps <- posterior_survfit(mod_sx,
  newdata = nd,
  times = 0,
  extrapolate = TRUE) |>
  suppressWarnings()
head(ps)
```




### 3. Plot
```{r}
panel_labels <- c('1' = "No Intervention", '2' = "Intervention performed")
pps <- plot(ps) +
  aes(colour = factor(id), fill = factor(id)) +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  facet_wrap(~ id, labeller = labeller(id = panel_labels)) +
           theme(axis.title.y = element_text(size=12, face="bold"), 
               axis.title.x = element_text(size=12, face="bold"),
               title = element_text(size=12, face="bold"),
               plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
               axis.text.x = element_text(color = "grey50", size = 10),
               axis.text.y = element_text(color = "grey50",size = 10)) +
            theme(strip.text.x = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold.italic"),
                   strip.background = element_rect(fill="white")
        )

print(pps)
```



## Check PH assumption visually
### make predictions of both the hazard and log hazard
```{r}
ph <- suppressWarnings(posterior_survfit(mod_sx, newdata = nd, type = "haz"))
pl <- suppressWarnings(posterior_survfit(mod_sx, newdata = nd, type = "loghaz"))

```



#### create plots
```{r}
pph <- plot(ph) +
  facet_wrap(~ id, labeller = labeller(id = panel_labels))
ppl <- plot(pl) +
  facet_wrap(~ id, labeller = labeller(id = panel_labels))
```



#### combine plots in grid and plot
```{r, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 8}
plot_grid(pph, ppl, ncol = 1)
```














# XIIa.  Bayesian multi-level survival analysis for effect of atenolol_pre with random intercept for centre and control set

## Set prior for beta variables
Set a neutral, weakly-regularising prior...
 ~ student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2.0)
```{r}
prior_beta_aten_pre <- student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 1.75, autoscale = c(FALSE, TRUE))
```

Based on the DAG, use the following adjustment variables: RV syst dys, referral centre.




## Fit model
NB use status ... rstanarm requires the dead animals to be classified as 1, whilst censored are 0.
```{r}
mod_aten_pre <- stan_surv(formula = Surv(tstart, tstop, status) ~ atenolol_pre
                      + s_tapse
                      + (1| centre),
  data = df,
  basehaz = "ms",
  prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 20, autoscale = FALSE),
  prior = prior_beta_aten_pre,
  prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
  iter    = 12000,
  warmup = 4000,
  chains = 4,
  cores = 4,
  adapt_delta = 0.99999,  # Often helpful for complex models
  control = list(max_treedepth = 20),
  init = 0.1,
  seed = 666)
```



## Summarise priors from model
```{r}
prior_summary(mod_aten_pre)
```



## Model summary
```{r}
summary(mod_aten_pre)
```



## Model short summary
```{r}

```


#### c. compute prior tail probability of posterior mean

### 4. Sensitivity analyses to assess robustness of results to choice of prior
#### a. create priors of different strength for s_vmaxav_vmaxpv variable
To determine whether the substantive conclusions depend upon the exact prior choice.

NB the scale variable is strengthened or weakened by multiplying or dividing the scale of the main prior by 2, respectively. The location is set to the posterior mean from the main model, to ensure that the priors are centred on a plausible value.
NB.  Had to use 0.5, 1, and 2 to ensure that the chains all completed.
```{r}
priors_bin <- list(
  weak = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 3.5, autoscale = FALSE),
  moderate = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 1.75, autoscale = FALSE),
  strong = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 0.825, autoscale = FALSE)
)
```




#### b. refit model with different priors and compare results
```{r}
fits <- lapply(priors_bin, function(p) {
  stan_surv(formula = Surv(tstart, tstop, status) ~ atenolol_pre
                      + s_tapse
                      + (1| centre),
            basehaz = "ms",
            data = df,
            prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 20, autoscale = FALSE),
            prior = p,
            prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
            iter    = 2000,
            chains = 4,
            cores = 4,
            adapt_delta = 0.99999,  # Often helpful for complex models
            control = list(max_treedepth = 20),
            init = 0.1,
            seed = 666
            )
})
```



#### c. compare posterior intervals for hazard ratios across different priors
```{r}
# calculate median hazard ratio across different priors
HR_med_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  posterior::as_draws_df(f) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    summarise(
      median = exp(quantile(atenolol_pre, probs = 0.5))
    )
})
HR_med <- c(HR_med_sens[[1]], HR_med_sens[[2]], HR_med_sens[[3]])


# calculate 89% credible interval for hazard ratio across different priors
HR_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  exp(posterior_interval(f, pars = "atenolol_pre", prob = 0.89))
})
```

# XIIb.  Bayesian multi-level survival analysis for effect of atenolol_post with random intercept for centre and control set

## Set prior for beta variables
Set a neutral, weakly-regularising prior...
 ~ student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2.0)
```{r}
prior_beta_aten_post <- student_t(df = 3, location = c(0, 0, 0), scale = c(2.0, 1.5, 1.5), autoscale = c(FALSE, FALSE, FALSE))
```

Based on the DAG, use the following adjustment variables: atenolol_pre, intervention (yes) and referral centre.




## Fit model
NB use status ... rstanarm requires the dead animals to be classified as 1, whilst censored are 0.
```{r}
mod_aten_post <- stan_surv(formula = Surv(tstart, tstop, status) ~ atenolol_post
                      + atenolol_pre
                      + surgery
                      + (1| centre),
  data = df,
  basehaz = "ms",
  prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 15, autoscale = FALSE),
  prior = prior_beta_aten_post,
  prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
  iter    = 12000,
  warmup = 4000,
  chains = 4,
  cores = 4,
  adapt_delta = 0.99999,  # Often helpful for complex models
  control = list(max_treedepth = 20),
  init = 0.1,
  seed = 666)
```

### 2. Check performance of prior probability
```{r}
mod_aten_post_prior_only <- update(mod_aten_post, prior_PD = TRUE)
```




### 3. Check prosterior vs prior for beta variable
#### a. extract draws for posterior and prior
```{r}
# extract draws
post_draws  <- as.matrix(mod_aten_post)
prior_draws <- as.matrix(mod_aten_post_prior_only)
```





#### b. plot marginal distributions for posterior and prior
``` {r}
# Compare marginal distributions
dens(post_draws[, "atenolol_post"], show.zero = TRUE, col = "red", main = "Neutral prior vs posterior for atenolol after procedure", xlab = "Beta coefficient for the effect of atenolol after procedure", xlim = c(-4, 4), ylim = c(0, 1.0))
dens(prior_draws[, "atenolol_post"], add=TRUE, col = "blue", show.zero = TRUE)
```



#### c. compute prior tail probability of posterior mean
If this probability is very small (e.g. < 0.05), the posterior lies in a region the prior considered implausible.
```{r}
beta_hat <- mean(post_draws[, "atenolol_post"])

mean(abs(prior_draws[, "atenolol_post"] - beta_hat) <
       abs(prior_draws[, "atenolol_post"] - mean(prior_draws[, "atenolol_post"])))

```




### 4. Sensitivity analyses to assess robustness of results to choice of prior
#### a. create priors of different strength for s_vmaxav_vmaxpv variable
To determine whether the substantive conclusions depend upon the exact prior choice.

NB the scale variable is strengthened or weakened by multiplying or dividing the scale of the main prior by 2, respectively. The location is set to the posterior mean from the main model, to ensure that the priors are centred on a plausible value.
NB.  Had to use 0.5, 1, and 2 to ensure that the chains all completed.
```{r}
priors_bin <- list(
  weak = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 4, autoscale = FALSE),
  moderate = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2, autoscale = FALSE),
  strong = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 1, autoscale = FALSE)
)
```




#### b. refit model with different priors and compare results
```{r}
fits <- lapply(priors_bin, function(p) {
  stan_surv(formula = Surv(tstart, tstop, status) ~ atenolol_post
                      + surgery
                      + atenolol_pre
                      + (1| centre),
            basehaz = "ms",
            data = df,
            prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 15, autoscale = FALSE),
            prior = p,
            prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
            iter    = 2000,
            chains = 4,
            cores = 4,
            adapt_delta = 0.99999,  # Often helpful for complex models
            control = list(max_treedepth = 20),
            init = 0.1,
            seed = 666
            )
})
```



#### c. compare posterior intervals for hazard ratios across different priors
```{r}
# calculate median hazard ratio across different priors
HR_med_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  posterior::as_draws_df(f) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    summarise(
      median = exp(quantile(atenolol_post, probs = 0.5))
    )
})
HR_med <- c(HR_med_sens[[1]], HR_med_sens[[2]], HR_med_sens[[3]])


# calculate 89% credible interval for hazard ratio across different priors
HR_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  exp(posterior_interval(f, pars = "atenolol_post", prob = 0.89))
})

# combine median and credible intervals into a summary table
HR_sens_summary <- rbind(HR_med, HR_sens)
row.names(HR_sens_summary) <- c("Median", "Lower", "Upper")

# transpose the table for better readability
HR_sens_summary
```

# XIII.  Bayesian multi-level survival analysis for effect of PROCEDURE TYPE with SEPARATE VARIABLES (balloon / stent) random intercept for centre and control set

## Set prior for beta variables
Set a neutral, weakly-regularising prior...
 ~ student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2.0)
```{r}
prior_beta_prtyp <- student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 1.5, autoscale = FALSE)
```

Based on the DAG, use the following adjustment variables: concurrent congen, referral centre, stenosis type (and sx yes).
NB need to use surgery df to ensure that the analysis is only on dogs that have had surgery.




## Fit model
NB use status ... rstanarm requires the dead animals to be classified as 1, whilst censored are 0.
```{r}
mod_prtyp <- stan_surv(formula = Surv(tstart, tstop, status) ~ balloon * stent
                        + concurrent_congenital
                        + type
                        + (1| centre),
  data = df_surg,
  basehaz = "ms",
  prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 15, autoscale = FALSE),
  prior = prior_beta_prtyp,
  prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
  iter    = 12000,
  warmup = 4000,
  chains = 4,
  cores = 4,
  adapt_delta = 0.999,  # Often helpful for complex models
  seed = 666)
```

### 3. Check prosterior vs prior for beta variable
#### a. extract draws for posterior and prior
```{r}
# extract draws
post_draws  <- as.matrix(mod_prtyp)
prior_draws <- as.matrix(mod_prtyp_prior_only)
```



#### b. Balloon
##### i. plot marginal distributions for posterior and prior
``` {r}
# Compare marginal distributions
dens(post_draws[, "balloon"], show.zero = TRUE, col = "red", main = "Comparison of prior and posterior for balloon valvulopasty", xlab = "Beta coefficient for the effect of balloon valvuloplasty", xlim = c(-5, 5), ylim = c(0, 0.5)) 
dens(prior_draws[, "balloon"], add=TRUE, col = "blue", show.zero = TRUE)
```



##### ii. compute prior tail probability of posterior mean
If this probability is very small (e.g. < 0.05), the posterior lies in a region the prior considered implausible.
```{r}
beta_hat <- mean(post_draws[, "balloon"])

mean(abs(prior_draws[, "balloon"] - beta_hat) <
       abs(prior_draws[, "balloon"] - mean(prior_draws[, "balloon"])))

```



#### c. Stent
##### i. plot marginal distributions for posterior and prior
``` {r}
# Compare marginal distributions
dens(post_draws[, "stent"], show.zero = TRUE, col = "red", main = "Comparison of prior and posterior for stent", xlab = "Beta coefficient for the effect of stent", xlim = c(-5, 5), ylim = c(0, 0.5)) 
dens(prior_draws[, "stent"], add=TRUE, col = "blue", show.zero = TRUE)
```



##### ii. compute prior tail probability of posterior mean
If this probability is very small (e.g. < 0.05), the posterior lies in a region the prior considered implausible.
```{r}
beta_hat <- mean(post_draws[, "stent"])

mean(abs(prior_draws[, "stent"] - beta_hat) <
       abs(prior_draws[, "stent"] - mean(prior_draws[, "stent"])))

```




#### d. Balloon then stent
##### i. plot marginal distributions for posterior and prior
``` {r}
# Compare marginal distributions
dens(post_draws[, "balloon:stent"], show.zero = TRUE, col = "red", main = "Comparison of prior and posterior for balloon and stent", xlab = "Beta coefficient for the effect of balloon and stent", xlim = c(-5, 5), ylim = c(0, 0.5)) 
dens(prior_draws[, "balloon:stent"], add=TRUE, col = "blue", show.zero = TRUE)
```



##### ii. compute prior tail probability of posterior mean
If this probability is very small (e.g. < 0.05), the posterior lies in a region the prior considered implausible.
```{r}
beta_hat <- mean(post_draws[, "balloon:stent"])

mean(abs(prior_draws[, "balloon:stent"] - beta_hat) <

```







### 4. Sensitivity analyses to assess robustness of results to choice of prior
#### a. create priors of different strength for s_vmaxav_vmaxpv variable
To determine whether the substantive conclusions depend upon the exact prior choice.

NB the scale variable is strengthened or weakened by multiplying or dividing the scale of the main prior by 2, respectively. The location is set to the posterior mean from the main model, to ensure that the priors are centred on a plausible value.
NB.  Had to use 0.5, 1, and 2 to ensure that the chains all completed.
```{r}
priors_bin <- list(
  weak = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 3, autoscale = FALSE),
  moderate = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 1.5, autoscale = FALSE),
  strong = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 0.75, autoscale = FALSE)
)
```




#### b. refit model with different priors and compare results
```{r}
fits <- lapply(priors_bin, function(p) {
  stan_surv(formula = Surv(tstart, tstop, status) ~ balloon * stent
                        + concurrent_congenital
                        + type
                        + (1| centre),
            basehaz = "ms",
            data = df_surg,
            prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 20, autoscale = FALSE),
            prior = p,
            prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
            iter    = 2000,
            chains = 4,
            cores = 4,
            adapt_delta = 0.99999,  # Often helpful for complex models
            control = list(max_treedepth = 20),
            init = 0.1,
            seed = 666
            )
})
```



#### c. compare posterior intervals for hazard ratios cross different priors
##### i. balloon
```{r}
# calculate median hazard ratio across different priors
HR_med_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  posterior::as_draws_df(f) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    summarise(
      median = exp(quantile(balloon, probs = 0.5))
    )
})
HR_med <- c(HR_med_sens[[1]], HR_med_sens[[2]], HR_med_sens[[3]])


# calculate 89% credible interval for hazard ratio across different priors
HR_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  exp(posterior_interval(f, pars = "balloon", prob = 0.89))
})

# combine median and credible intervals into a summary table
HR_sens_summary <- rbind(HR_med, HR_sens)
row.names(HR_sens_summary) <- c("Median", "Lower", "Upper")

# transpose the table for better readability
HR_sens_summary
```

# XIV.  Bayesian multi-level survival analysis for effect of COMPLICATIONS with random intercept for centre and control set

## Set prior for beta variables
Set a neutral, weakly-regularising prior...
 ~ student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2.0)
```{r}
prior_beta_comp <- student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2.0, autoscale = FALSE)
```

Based on the DAG, use the following adjustment variables: high pressure, low pressure, referral centre, stent.
NB need to include balloon type here as well for an appropriate adjustment set




## Need to create separate variables for high pressure and low pressure so as to model complications appropriately
```{r}
df_surg$high_pressure <- ifelse(df_surg$balloon_type == "high_pressure", 1, 0)
df_surg$high_pressure[is.na(df_surg$high_pressure)] <- 0
df_surg$low_pressure <- ifelse(df_surg$balloon_type == "low_pressure", 1, 0)
df_surg$low_pressure[is.na(df_surg$low_pressure)] <- 0
```




## Fit model
NB use status ... rstanarm requires the dead animals to be classified as 1, whilst censored are 0.
```{r}
mod_comp <- stan_surv(formula = Surv(tstart, tstop, status) ~ complications
                      + stent
                      + high_pressure
                      + low_pressure
                      + (1| centre),
  data = df_surg,
  basehaz = "ms",
  prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 20, autoscale = FALSE),
  prior = prior_beta_comp,
  prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
  iter    = 12000,
  warmup = 4000,
  chains = 4,
  cores = 4,
  adapt_delta = 0.9999,  # Often helpful for complex models
  seed = 666)
```

```{r}
prior_summary(mod_comp)
```


# XVII.  Bayesian multi-level survival analysis for effect of BALLOON TYPE with random intercept for centre
Have conditioned on balloon use... by using the df_balloon dataset which only includes dogs that had a balloon procedure.  This conditions on surgery (only including those that had a procedure, and then use of balloon in procedure_type) Therefore, no control set required (other than including centre as a grouping variable) for the causal effect to be estimated.

## Neutral prior for clinicial signs
No prior information on the effect of clinical signs
Therefore, set a Neutral weekly regularising prior...
 ~ student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2.5)
```{r}
prior_balloon_type <- student_t(df = 3, location = c(0, 0, 0), scale = c(2.0, 1.75, 1.75), autoscale = c(FALSE, FALSE, FALSE))
```

Based on the DAG, use the following adjustment variables: proc type, referral centre, stenosis type.
NB to include procedure type, simply use df_balloon as that will ensure anaylsis only includes dogs that had a balloon procedure.



## Fit model
NB use status ... rstanarm requires the dead animals to be classified as 1, whilst censored are 0.
```{r}
mod_balloon_type <- stan_surv(formula = Surv(tstart, tstop, status)  ~ balloon_type
                              + type
                              + (1| centre),
  data = df_balloon,
  basehaz = "ms",
  prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 10, autoscale = FALSE),
  prior = prior_balloon_type,
  prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
  iter    = 12000,
  warmup = 4000,
  chains = 4,
  cores = 4,
  adapt_delta = 0.9999,  # Often helpful for complex models
  seed = 666)
```




## Summarise priors from model
```{r}
prior_summary(mod_balloon_type)
```



## Model summary
```{r}
summary(mod_balloon_type)
```



## Model short summary
```{r}
print(mod_balloon_type, digits = 3)
```



## Plot Baseline hazard of model
```{r}
plot(mod_balloon_type)
```



## Plots of model convergences

## Get results
```{r}
posterior_mod_balloon_type <- as.array(mod_balloon_type)
```

``` {r}
dens(prior_draws[, "balloon_typehigh_pressure"], add=TRUE, col = "blue", show.zero = TRUE)
```



#### c. compute prior tail probability of posterior mean
If this probability is very small (e.g. < 0.05), the posterior lies in a region the prior considered implausible.
```{r}
beta_hat <- mean(post_draws[, "balloon_typehigh_pressure"])

mean(abs(prior_draws[, "balloon_typehigh_pressure"] - beta_hat) <
       abs(prior_draws[, "balloon_typehigh_pressure"] - mean(prior_draws[, "balloon_typehigh_pressure"])))

```





### 4. Sensitivity analyses to assess robustness of results to choice of prior
#### a. create priors of different strength for balloon type variable
To determine whether the substantive conclusions depend upon the exact prior choice.

NB the scale variable is strengthened or weakened by multiplying or dividing the scale of the main prior by 2, respectively. The location is set to the posterior mean from the main model, to ensure that the priors are centred on a plausible value.
NB.  Had to use 0.5, 1, and 2 to ensure that the chains all completed.
```{r}
priors_bin <- list(
  weak = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 4, autoscale = FALSE),
  moderate = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2, autoscale = FALSE),
  strong = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 1, autoscale = FALSE)
)
```




#### b. refit model with different priors and compare results
```{r}
fits <- lapply(priors_bin, function(p) {
  stan_surv(formula = Surv(tstart, tstop, status) ~ balloon_type
                              + type
                              + (1| centre),
            basehaz = "ms",
            data = df_balloon,
            prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 20, autoscale = FALSE),
            prior = p,
            prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
            iter    = 2000,
            chains = 4,
            cores = 4,
            adapt_delta = 0.9999,  # Often helpful for complex models
            control = list(max_treedepth = 20),
            init = 0.1,
            seed = 666
            )
})
```



#### c. compare posterior intervals for hazard ratios acxross different priors
```{r}
# calculate median hazard ratio across different priors
HR_med_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  posterior::as_draws_df(f) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    summarise(
      median = exp(quantile(balloon_typehigh_pressure, probs = 0.5))
    )
})
HR_med <- c(HR_med_sens[[1]], HR_med_sens[[2]], HR_med_sens[[3]])


# calculate 89% credible interval for hazard ratio across different priors
HR_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  exp(posterior_interval(f, pars = "balloon_typehigh_pressure", prob = 0.89))
})

# combine median and credible intervals into a summary table
HR_sens_summary <- rbind(HR_med, HR_sens)
row.names(HR_sens_summary) <- c("Median", "Lower", "Upper")

# transpose the table for better readability
HR_sens_summary
```

## Set prior for beta variables
Set an informative prior...
 ~ student_t(df = 3, location = -0.879165, scale = 0.2911939)
 
```{r}
prior_beta_sx2 <- student_t(df = 3, location = c(-0.879165, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0),
                           scale = c(0.29119395, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1),
                           autoscale = c(FALSE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE))
```
NB needed to set a tighter scale variable for prior_intercept and also prior_beta_sx in order to improve regularisation and resolve divergent transitions.

Based on the DAG, use the following adjustment variables: age, clin signs, concurrent congen, pressure grad, referral centre, stenosis type.




## Fit model with for surgery (plus correction set)
NB use status ... rstanarm requires the dead animals to be classified as 1, whilst censored are 0.
```{r}
mod_sx2 <- stan_surv(formula = Surv(tstart, tstop, status) ~ surgery
                    + s_age
                    + concurrent_congenital
                    + type
                    + clinical_signs
                    + s_pv_max_pg
                    + (1| centre),
  data = df,
  basehaz = "ms",
  prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 15, autoscale = FALSE),
  prior = prior_beta_sx2,
  prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
  iter    = 12000,
  warmup = 4000,
  chains = 4,
  cores = 4,
  adapt_delta = 0.9999,  # Often helpful for complex models
  seed = 666)

```

#### c. compute prior tail probability of posterior mean
If this probability is very small (e.g. < 0.05), the posterior lies in a region the prior considered implausible.
```{r}

mean(abs(prior_draws[, "atenolol_pre"] - beta_hat) <

```




### 4. Sensitivity analyses to assess robustness of results to choice of prior
#### a. create priors of different strength for s_vmaxav_vmaxpv variable
To determine whether the substantive conclusions depend upon the exact prior choice.

NB the scale variable is strengthened or weakened by multiplying or dividing the scale of the main prior by 2, respectively. The location is set to the posterior mean from the main model, to ensure that the priors are centred on a plausible value.
NB.  Had to use 0.5, 1, and 2 to ensure that the chains all completed.
```{r}
priors_bin <- list(
  weak = student_t(df = 3, location = 1.866284, scale = 1.6887696, autoscale = FALSE),
  moderate = student_t(df = 3, location = 1.866284, scale = 0.8443848, autoscale = FALSE),
  strong = student_t(df = 3, location = 1.866284, scale = 0.4221924, autoscale = FALSE)
)
```

 c(1.866284, 0), scale = c(0.8443848, 1.5),


#### b. refit model with different priors and compare results
```{r}
fits <- lapply(priors_bin, function(p) {
  stan_surv(formula = Surv(tstart, tstop, status) ~ atenolol_pre
                      + s_tapse
                      + (1| centre),
            basehaz = "ms",
            data = df,
            prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 20, autoscale = FALSE),
            prior = p,
            prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
            iter    = 2000,
            chains = 4,
            cores = 4,
            adapt_delta = 0.99999,  # Often helpful for complex models
            control = list(max_treedepth = 20),
            init = 0.1,
            seed = 666
            )
})
```



#### c. compare posterior intervals for hazard ratios across different priors
```{r}
# calculate median hazard ratio across different priors
HR_med_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  posterior::as_draws_df(f) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    summarise(
      median = exp(quantile(atenolol_pre, probs = 0.5))
    )
})
HR_med <- c(HR_med_sens[[1]], HR_med_sens[[2]], HR_med_sens[[3]])


# calculate 89% credible interval for hazard ratio across different priors
HR_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  exp(posterior_interval(f, pars = "atenolol_pre", prob = 0.89))
})

# combine median and credible intervals into a summary table
HR_sens_summary <- rbind(HR_med, HR_sens)
row.names(HR_sens_summary) <- c("Median", "Lower", "Upper")

# transpose the table for better readability
HR_sens_summary
```

# XIIb. version 2.
# Bayesian multi-level survival analysis for effect of atenolol_post with random intercept for centre and control set

## Set prior for beta variables
Set an informative prior...
 ~ student_t(df = 3, location = 1.866284, scale = 0.8443848)
 
```{r}
prior_beta_aten_post2 <- student_t(df = 3, location = c(1.866284, 1.866284, 0), scale = c(0.8443848, 0.8443848, 2), autoscale = c(FALSE, FALSE, FALSE))
```
 
Based on the DAG, use the following adjustment variables: RV syst dys, referral centre.





## Fit model
NB use status ... rstanarm requires the dead animals to be classified as 1, whilst censored are 0.
```{r}
mod_aten_post2 <- stan_surv(formula = Surv(tstart, tstop, status) ~ atenolol_post
                      + atenolol_pre
                      + surgery
                      + (1| centre),
  data = df,
  basehaz = "ms",
  prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 20, autoscale = FALSE),
  prior = prior_beta_aten_post2,
  prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
  iter    = 12000,
  warmup = 4000,
  chains = 4,
  cores = 4,
  adapt_delta = 0.99999,  # Often helpful for complex models
  control = list(max_treedepth = 20),
  init = 0.1,
  seed = 666)
```
